chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with him - from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari and Sa'd ibn Abdullah, and Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, a prominent early Shia scholar and narrator
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ الْحِمْيَرِ: Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى: Muhammad ibn Musa, a key transmitter in the chain

ai.seo_question: How is the chain of narration for Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub's hadiths traced in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a detailed biographical cross-reference to authenticate the reliability of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, a key figure in the Kufan school of hadith. By tracing the chain through prominent companions like Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, he demonstrates the rigorous verification process (ilm al-rijal) essential for establishing the authenticity of Imami traditions.
